newsitem.title: USA: Minn Senate advances gas tax hike for road repairs.
newsitem.headline: Minn Senate advances gas tax hike for road repairs.

text.p: The Minnesota Senate approved a 4-cent-per-gallon gasoline tax increase and a temporary one-cent increase to repair roads damaged by flooding.
Senators voted 34-31 on Monday to approve the gasoline tax increase, said Andre Colaiace, administrator for the House transportation committee.
The Senate has passed gasoline tax increases several times in recent years, but the proposals have failed to receive support from either representatives or the governor, Colaiace noted.

Under the Senate plan, a temporary one-cent increase would generate about $27 million for road repairs in counties that sustained flood damage only, Colaiace said. The increase would begin on July 1 and run through June 30, 1998, he said.

The permanent increase would begin with a two-cent hike on July 1 and a second two-cent increase on July 1, 1998, Colaiace said. Estimated revenues from the permanent increase would be $108 million, he said.
The Senate proposal conflicts with a transportation funding package passed earlier by the House, likely sending the matter into a conference committee, Colaiace said.

The bill also includes funding to hire 50 state troopers and a 0.25 percent sales tax increase in the Minneapolis-St. Paul metropolitan area, Colaiace said. The sales tax increase would replace the property tax portion of funding for transit operations, he said.
Minnesota Gov. Arne Carlson has said he would support increasing the number of state troopers, but has also said he would veto any measure that includes a sales tax increase.
